messages.subject: Blavaan does not run Stan on macOS Catalina while Rstan and brms works fine.
parts:
Hello,
I have an issue running the Blavaan bcfa() function using the following environment. I wonder if you could help with this.

Environment:
R version 3.6.3 (2020-02-29)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 (64-bit)

Does anyone have any idea what the problems are and how to fix this?

parts:
Masaki

I couple of ideas to test,
- if you loaded blavaan ahead of the model, dont use :: to call the bcfa function ( blavaan::bcfa ), just use bcfa
- You have very strict priors on the factor loadings, basically you are saying that all the factor loadings are ver close to 0
- Try running the example from the help page for the bcfa function ?bcfa, this is a simple model that we know it works. If this fails might be an issue with the installation of blavaan. But is this model works, and yours is not working, might be an issue with you data or model. Would help use narrow down were the problem might be

# The Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(fit)

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Blavaan does not run Stan on macOS Catalina while Rstan and brms works fine.
parts:
Masaki,

My first guess is a versioning issue: your R version is somewhat old (pre 4.0), and it looks like you are using a development version of rstan (I believe that 2.21.2 is the newest version on CRAN). I personally haven't tested blavaan on the versions that you are using. If you installed rstan 2.21.3 after you installed blavaan, you might have to re-install blavaan so that it gets compiled with rstan 2.21.3.

Or, if you can, I might try the most up-to-date version of R paired with package versions on CRAN. But I realize you might have other reasons for using the versions you are using.

Ed
